individual_agents.bio: Mohamed Nor is a prominent real estate agent in Mogadishu whose phone rings constantly from property hunters wanting to own a piece of Mogadishu. He operates from an airy office in the battle-scarred Somali capital, serving clients who want to invest in Mogadishu real estate. His success stems from the real estate boom following security improvements after the ouster of al-Shabab.

individual_agents.bio: Liban Hashi is a real estate agent in Mogadishu who describes the property market as simply 'good business.' He has witnessed property prices more than quadruple in just a couple of years in Mogadishu. Like his colleague Mohamed Nor, he can make up to $10,000 in commissions weekly, compared to what they used to earn yearly when Mogadishu was under al-Shabab control.
individual_agents.market_insight: Property prices have more than quadrupled in recent years due to improved security. Expert on property price trends and market dynamics

data_limitations.note: Somalia's real estate market is largely informal with limited online professional disclosure. Many professionals operate through personal networks, word-of-mouth referrals, and street-level information gathering rather than formal marketing channels.
data_limitations.market_characteristics: Properties not advertised in media; agents obtain information by walking streets and seeking potential sellers
data_limitations.recommendation: For comprehensive data collection, direct outreach to local real estate professionals, chambers of commerce, and informal market networks would be necessary.
